title: Global Impact — Ring Platform
description: Ring as an implied ultimate weapon of peace: open technology given freely to goodwill communities so they can focus on local needs inside their own ecosystem of values.

hero.title: Technology that turns attention into peace work
hero.subtitle: Ring is offered freely to any goodwill community on the planet. Clone it, brand it in your values, and use AI matching plus a local money stack so neighbors can solve local needs together — instead of being pulled into noise, scarcity theater, and distant platforms that extract attention without returning sovereignty.

thesis.title: Why Ring exists globally
thesis.description: War, poverty, and fragmentation thrive when people cannot coordinate. Ring’s implied purpose is peaceful: give communities a complete digital commons — opportunities, messaging, store, credits, sponsored native token, MicroDAO votes, NFT gates — so they can focus on what is near and real. Not another feed. A shared operating system for local abundance.
thesis.quote: From darkness toward light: open tools, local ownership, collective focus — peace as practiced coordination, not a slogan.

effects.title: Global effects of a free Ring
effects.subtitle: When every goodwill community can host its own Ring, the planet gains many small centers of relevant action instead of one extractive center of distraction.

sovereignty.title: Technological sovereignty
sovereignty.description: Communities run their own clone — their branding, their token, their membership rules, their data posture. Values stay local; the stack stays modern.

focus.title: Collective focus on local needs
focus.description: AI matching notifies the right people about nearby opportunities. Less scrolling past the world; more showing up for the street, the school, the clinic, the farm, the workshop.

economy.title: An ecosystem of values that can settle
economy.description: Credit rewards, Token Desk, sponsored SPL transfers, MicroDAO native-token votes, and NFT gates let a community circulate value without forcing everyone to hold chain gas or abandon their cultural economics.

peace.title: Peace as capacity, not performance
peace.description: Weapons of war destroy coordination. A weapon of peace multiplies it: open-source Ring lowers the cost of standing up honest markets, mutual aid, and transparent priority voting wherever goodwill already exists.

replication.title: Replication without permission theater
replication.description: Goodwill groups should not wait for venture approval to organize. Clone, configure, deploy — then invite neighbors into an ecosystem that answers to them.

education.title: Learning by building the commons
education.description: Students and builders learn modern stacks while shipping real community infrastructure — the path from poverty of tools to prosperity of capability.

howItWorks.title: How a community turns Ring into local impact

step1.title: Receive the commons
step1.description: Take the open Ring platform — documentation, clone path, and white-label config — as a gift of capability, not a lease on attention.

step2.title: Root it in your values
step2.description: Set display name, locales, membership, native token, and modules so the system speaks your community’s language and rules.

step3.title: Match needs to people
step3.description: Post opportunities and let AI notify relevant members. Contribution earns credit-balance rewards under published, non-speculative rules.

step4.title: Settle and decide together
step4.description: Use Token Desk, gasless sends, MicroDAO native-token votes, and NFT gates so priorities and access stay inside your ecosystem — transparent, local, and actionable.

cta.title: Carry the light outward
cta.subtitle: Read the publisher story, then start a clone path for your community — or for the next goodwill network that needs its own Ring.
